newsitem.title: USA: Delta has no shortage of CEO candidates.
newsitem.headline: Delta has no shortage of CEO candidates.

text.p: Delta Air Lines Inc would have little trouble finding qualified candidates to replace Ron Allen as chief executive when he retires on July 31, analysts and executives said Tuesday.

The roster of corporate talent ranges from Chief Financial Officer Thomas Roeck and Delta board member Gerald Grinstein to the heirs apparent at Continental Airlines Inc and American Airlines parent, AMR Corp.
Analysts also pointed to a clutch of independent figures, including former presidents of Delta and UAL Corp.
Analysts who attended a Tuesday meeting with Delta executives in New York were frustrated by the company's continued reticence about Allen's departure.
A Delta statement issued on Monday said the No. 3 ranked U.S. carrier would look both inside and out for a successor and that it would stick to a strategy of seeking disciplined internal growth.

By the next morning, analysts said, the company was prepared to share little else about the situation and declined comment on speculation about a possible resumption of its one-time merger talks with Continental.
Allen himself later refused to respond to questions from a Reuter correspondent as he left the meeting with analysts.

"When you're CEO, you have a lot of different constituencies. If you're not taking care of the daily feeding of each group, then you're probably not going to be a happy camper," said Helane Becker, an analyst with Smith Barney.

Press reports about the departure referred to clashes between Allen and board directors. Many said Allen clashed with Grinstein, former head of Western Airlines, after seeking to replace Roeck. Roeck had worked with Grinstein at Western Airlines until the carrier was bought by Delta in 1987.
A Delta spokesman Tuesday had no comment on the reports.

Meanwhile, analysts said Grinstein himself would have the experience to step in for Allen on an interim basis. Some also saw Roeck as a possible successor in the company, where there has been no clear-cut No. 2 to Allen for some years.
Outside figures seen by analysts and industry executives to have the charisma and wherewithal to lead Delta include:
-- Gregory Brenneman, the chief operating officer at Continental;
-- Former Air Canada Chief Executive and Delta President Hollis Harris;
-- Raymond Vecci, former Alaska Airlines CEO.
